summary: In Greek mythology, Amphion (Ancient Greek Ἀμφίων) son of Iasus is the Minyan king who once ruled mightily in Orchomenus and fathered Chloris, youngest of his daughters — the queen Homer's Odysseus sees as Neleus' wife in the underworld. Distinct from Amphion the Theban wall-builder, twin of Zethus, and from the Argonaut Amphion of Pellene.
etymology: Ancient Greek Ἀμφίων; several unrelated mythological men share the name.

sections.heading: King of Minyan Orchomenus
paragraphs: In Odyssey 11.281–286 Odysseus names Chloris, whom Neleus wedded for her beauty after countless bridal gifts: she was youngest daughter of Amphion son of Iasus, who once ruled mightily in Orchomenus of the Minyae. By Neleus she bore Nestor, Chromius, Periclymenus, and Pero. Apollodorus follows the same Chloris–Neleus marriage; some scholia name Persephone daughter of Minyas as Amphion's wife and add Phylomache (wife of Pelias) among his daughters.

Diodorus and Hyginus sometimes make Chloris a surviving Niobid of the Theban Amphion — a conflation Homer and Apollodorus avoid. Pausanias remembers Amphion in the Orchomenian landscape of Minyas' treasury. This atlas entry is the Minyan king alone.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id amphion-orchomenus is Iasus' Orchomenian king alone. Distinct from amphion (Zeus' Theban lyre-builder, husband of Niobe) and from amphion-pella (Argonaut from Pellene).
